subject: Future Tech
title: Mining the Moon
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Mining the Moon.

hook.text: Lunar soil is rich in silicon, iron, titanium, and aluminum.

buildup.text: Regolith can be sintered by concentrated sunlight into bricks or melted into glass for habitat construction.

discovery.text: 3D printing with regolith was tested on Earth using simulated lunar soil.

twist.text: Lunar dust is razor-sharp and clings to everything via static charge. It damaged Apollo spacesuits in just three days.

climax.text: Solving the dust problem is critical. Coatings, air locks, and electrostatic shields are all being engineered right now.

punchline.text: The Moon's greatest resource is also its worst hazard.

quiz.question: Why is lunar dust dangerous to equipment and spacesuits?
options: It's razor-sharp and clings via static
